inputs.name: ftp
inputs.summary: Reads the files of one directory of an FTP server whose names match a glob, one message per file, once per run (FTPS unless the operator allows plain FTP).

fields.description: The FTP server as host or host:port, for example files.example.org:21; port 21 when left out.

How the connection is protected, for example explicit. explicit (the default) speaks FTPS: AUTH TLS, with the data channel protected too. none is plain FTP, which sends the password in the clear: the runner refuses it unless the operator has turned on your organization's allow_plain_ftp quota.
PEM certificates to trust besides the system ones, for a server signed by a private CA, for example -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- … -----END CERTIFICATE-----.
The login name, for example exports; anonymous when left empty.
The password, picked from the project's secrets, for example FTP_PASSWORD; the platform refuses a password typed in. Leave empty for an anonymous login.
The directory and a file-name glob, for example /exports/*.csv: every file in /exports whose name ends in .csv is read.
Delete each file from the server once the pipeline has handled it, for example for a drop folder. Not together with processed suffix.
Rename each handled file by adding this ending, for example .done; later runs skip the renamed files. Not together with delete on finish.
The largest file read, in bytes, from 1 to 268435456 (256 MiB), for example 33554432 for 32 MiB; a larger file fails the run.
The most files read in one run, from 1 to 10000, for example 100; the rest wait for the next run.
How long one server operation may take, up to 5m, for example 30s.

inputs.name: imap
inputs.summary: Reads the attachments of unread mails in one mailbox over IMAPS, one message per attachment, once per run; a mail is marked read or moved only after the pipeline handled it.

fields.description: The mail server as host or host:port, for example imap.example.org:993; port 993 when left out. IMAPS only, never plain IMAP.
PEM certificates to trust besides the system ones, for a server signed by a private CA, for example -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- … -----END CERTIFICATE-----.
The mailbox login, for example exports@city.example.org.
The password, picked from the project's secrets, for example IMAP_PASSWORD; the platform refuses a password typed in.
The folder to read, for example INBOX or INBOX/Exports; INBOX when left empty.
Only mails from this one sender address, for example exports@stat.example.org; any sender when left empty.
Only mails whose subject matches this regular expression, for example ^Daily traffic export; any subject when left empty.
Only attachments whose file name matches this glob, for example *.xlsx; every attachment when left empty.
What happens to a mail once the pipeline handled every attachment it gave, for example seen: seen marks it read, move moves it to the folder in move to.
With after ack move: the folder to move handled mails to, for example INBOX/Processed.
The largest attachment read, in bytes, from 1 to 268435456 (256 MiB), for example 26214400 for 25 MiB; a larger one is skipped.
The most mails read in one run, from 1 to 1000, for example 50; the rest wait for the next run.
How long one server operation may take, up to 5m, for example 30s.
